# Design system

Enforceable rules here; implementation detail in `docs/context/ui.md`; product intent in `PRODUCT.md`.

## Direction

PoGo Leiria is a product system for players using their phone outdoors in bright light, often one-handed and in a hurry. The visual language is dark, high-contrast, and precise, with a restrained **ember** interaction color and warm signal-gold for discovery and progress. It is adjacent to the game, not a replica of it.

Ember is a brick red, `oklch(0.52 0.17 28)`. It was called `blue` for a long time while rendering red, alongside a `blue-glow` that was salmon and a `cyan` that was pale cream; the names have been corrected to match what the values always were.

## Public contract

Apps consume `@pogoleiria/ui/tokens.css` and components from `@pogoleiria/ui`. Use semantic roles first: `background`, `foreground`, `card`, `muted`, `primary`, `accent`, `destructive`, `border`, `input`, and `ring`. The `surface-*`, `ink-*`, and named accent tokens are compatibility aliases for product-specific composition.

The token layers are:

1. Primitive palette: private tone and brand values in `:root`.
2. Semantic roles: app-facing meaning and theme contract.
3. Tailwind aliases: utility-friendly names for existing consumers.
4. Component APIs: accessible, touch-sized patterns with `data-slot` hooks.

## Usage rules

- Keep interactive targets at least 44px (`--control-min`).
- **Separate surfaces with light, not shadow.** `sunken` -> `background` -> `surface-raised` is a real lightness ramp, and `--border` sits well above the panel it outlines. `--shadow-float` is the only shadow, and it belongs to things that genuinely float: `AppSwitcher` and popovers. A drop shadow on a dark panel over a dark page is invisible in the sunlight these apps are used in. The hand-rolled panel shadows are gone: `.header-badge`, `.header-badge--active` and `.quest-reward-tile` keep their 2px rings but no drop component, and the shiny map's floating chrome uses `--shadow-float` like `AppSwitcher`.
- **Gold means a reward, progress toward one, or the active Início navigation item** (owner, 2026-10-14). It marked rewards, header figures and count badges at once, and so distinguished nothing; counts are `ink-label` now, ordinary figures are `ink-bright`, and a count on an icon is `CountDot`, neutral (`bg-ink-bright text-surface-sunken`) and never gold (owner, 2026-10-17): a count of matching rows is not a reward. The hub's `ShinyCard` keeps its gold border, tint and hover — a shiny is a reward — but its "Abrir Pokédex" CTA is neutral (`text-ink-label`, `group-hover:text-ink-bright`), like the raid hero's "Ver no mapa".
- **Ember means what you touch**: selected, pressed, focused. Quests category selections use the same flat ember fill; category identity stays in the coloured dot, rather than the button border. White on `--color-ember` measures 4.97:1, so a filled control carries its own label without a glow.
- **Each tool has an accent, used in one place** (owner, 2026-10-14): the switcher’s current item and icon take `--color-tool-home` (gold), `--color-tool-map` (teal), `--color-tool-quests` (Pokéstop blue) or `--color-tool-pokedex` (red), so where you are reads before the label does. Everything else you touch stays ember.
- **Discord purple opens Discord, and only that.** `--color-discord` (Discord's own `#5865F2`) is the message button to a trainer: Discord's mark alone on a 44px disc, no words (owner, 2026-10-11). Filled for someone offering an extra, tinted (`bg-discord/20`, `text-discord-bright`) for someone who is only being asked. In ember, a list of trainers was a column of red; red stays the colour of the suite's own controls.
- **Urgent means it runs out soon, and only that.** `--urgent` is an orange, `oklch(0.75 0.165 58)`, and it belongs on a countdown that has reached its last day, its last hour, its last few minutes. It is not `destructive`: nothing has gone wrong and nothing is being lost, the clock has simply run down. It is not gold either, because an event ending is not a reward. Hue 58 sits 30° from ember and 30° from gold so it reads as neither, and it measures 8.82:1 on `--background` and 8.01:1 on `--color-surface-raised`. It only works while it is rare: a section where *everything* is expiring says so with its own label, not by turning every row orange.
- **`--success` is a semantic role**, `--color-success` (from the private `--success-400`): the positive dot the hub's `LiveDot` draws, in place of a raw oklch literal. Like `--urgent`, it exists so a meaning has a name.
- **The hub's type scale is seven steps, declared as tokens** in `apps/landing/app/globals.css`: `micro` 10, `label` 11, `body` 13, `tier` 15, `title` 17, `figure` 19, `hero` 44 (plus `figure-lg` 22 and `hero-lg` 56). It had drifted to seventeen sizes across sixty-three call sites, including 10/10.5, 11/11.5, 12/12.5 and 18/19 — half a pixel is not a hierarchy step. Where a size steps up at `lg` it steps to the next token, never to a new invented value. A test fails on any `text-[Npx]` left in the hub.
- **One figure gets the big jump.** `hero` is the live Pokémon count on the map card and nothing else. Everything else sits between 10 and 19, so the ratio between the page's subject and its supporting text is ~2.3, not the 1.7 it was. The map figure steps `text-hero lg:text-hero-lg` (44 -> 56); `MapFiguresSkeleton` keeps the same height.
- **Section labels carry two levels, not one.** `SectionHeader`'s `tone`: `live` (things that expire — raids, Rocket, Max Battles, lures) is `font-display figure/figure-lg extrabold ink-bright`; `ambient` (things still true tonight) is the same size in `ink-label`, and is the default. The shared `SectionLabel` carries the same two named levels (D7, owner 2026-10-17) — `tone: 'live' | 'ambient'`, `ambient` by default — plus an optional `count` slot that sits opposite the label in the display face. The two levels are carried by colour alone at `figure` size since Holofote (2026-09-23).
- **`.lit` (in `tokens.css`) is the positive half of the light rule.** A 1px inset top highlight, `inset 0 1px 0 oklch(1 0 0 / 0.07)`, on raised panels. The suite banned drop shadows and then left every panel a flat fill inside a hairline, six down the page. This is not `--shadow-float`, which stays the only shadow and stays on things that float; it is the top edge of a surface catching the light, the same idiom `tab-pill` already used.
- **Set figures in `font-display` with `tabular-nums`** — counts, ratios, percentages. Digits then line up between one row and the next.
- Radius steps run 8 / 12 / 16 / 20 / 24, all five declared. A control sits one step tighter than the surface holding it. Desktop standalone buttons, inputs and menu rows use `radius-lg` (16px); cards and the desktop navigation container use `radius-xl` (20px). Use tokens instead of 18px/22px overrides. Search fields, textareas, tile actions, popup actions and generic tabs follow the same desktop control radius; hub, community, profile and quest card surfaces follow the desktop card radius. Joined filters and chips retain the shared pill geometry. **Phone cards are 24px** (D1, owner 2026-10-17): the phone card surfaces (Offline/Quiet notice, `error.tsx`, the folded raid panel, the Quests category dropdown, the raid hero, event cards, sprite chips, the shiny card and the profile stats) all use `rounded-2xl`, keeping their `lg:rounded-xl` desktop step. Controls and buttons keep their own radius.
- Use `text-foreground` for primary copy and `text-muted-foreground` for supporting copy. Do not invent one-off neutral colors.
- Use `primary` for actions and selected state, `accent` for attention/progress, and `destructive` for irreversible or invalid states.
- Prefer `Button`, `Input`, `SearchField`, `Tabs`, `Badge`, `Card`, `Progress`, `AppSwitcher`, `BackLink`, `CountDot`, `EmptyState`, `SectionLabel`, and shell components before composing new controls. Unused primitives are removed, not carried: `StatHeader` and `CountBadge` went the same way as Dialog (0 consumers, 2026-10-17); counts use `CountDot` and section labels use `SectionLabel`.
- Joined choices use `SegmentedControl`: rounded outer ends, level labels, a 1px divider tilted 8°, and an ember fill following the same join (owner's approved B preview). Use it for navigation, tabs, segmented filters and split actions. Separate chips and standalone buttons keep their own rounded shape. Selection stays in `aria-current`, `aria-pressed` or Radix `data-state`; geometry belongs to the shared component and `tokens.css`.
- **`BackLink` is the one back affordance**: a ChevronLeft and a word, 44px tall, `text-ink-label`, for both a navigation `href` and a sheet `onClick`. Sheet-internal icon backs use `ChevronLeft` consistently; six patterns had grown for one job.
- **`EmptyState`'s title is never smaller than its description**: title `text-body font-semibold ink-bright`, description `text-label ink-muted`.
- **`Progress` defaults to a gold fill on a sunken track** (`bg-gold` on `bg-surface-sunken`); consumers no longer override its colour.
- **The hub's three folds share one summary**, `MoreToggle` (`apps/landing/components/more-toggle.tsx`): a plain hairline row in `text-label font-semibold text-ink-label` with a ChevronDown and the caller's "Mais n / Menos", not the bordered box the events used or the muted aside the raid chips did.
- **One focus treatment, `outline-ember-bright`**: `focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-ember-bright` (plus `outline-offset-2` on buttons and badges), replacing the mixed 3px `ring-ring/50`, `ring-2 ring-ring` and `outline-ring` treatments.
- Navigation between the three tools belongs to `AppSwitcher`, in every app, and nothing else goes in it.
- **Desktop shell and folded generations use the owner’s I direction** (2026-10-13): the D navbar, one brand artwork at 18% with a soft fade toward the right and no small square logo, and the mobile’s uppercase Figtree wordmark (900, tight spacing, upright). Selected desktop navigation uses a flat solid tool accent with dark text, without a gradient, highlight or separate icon fill. Generation headers use compact F artwork at the right, regional tint and collection progress. Their border uses the shared neutral hairline at rest and neutral hairline-hover on hover; regional colour does not outline the control. The individual Pokémon rows remain unboxed; opening a generation keeps the card and artwork dimensions, and the expanded header stays pinned. The Megas view draws each generation with that same card (`GenerationHeading`), never a plain row, so a Mega sits where a Pokémon would.
- **Pokédex filters live in the desktop sidebar**, beneath search and above the category progress list, like Quests. Mobile search and filters remain in the dock. Label the groups Mostrar, Costumes and Lendários; the Categoria picker appears only in Procura/Para troca. Put Limpar filtros beside the filter heading. Collection progress defaults folded below 1100px viewport height and can always be opened; its summary keeps the percentage visible. Quests labels Recompensas and expands Categorias inside the sidebar, with ember-red selected Leiria/Marinha and Quests/Mapa controls and the same reset action.
- **On a phone, a tool's own controls live in its dock** (owner, 2026-10-11): `Dock` from `@pogoleiria/ui`, one floating bar above the switcher holding the search, a filters button, and the page's one or two ways out. What a dock button opens (`.dock-panel`) opens above it. The top of a phone screen is the title and the list; on the Pokédex the controls had grown to four fifths of the first screen. From `lg` the same controls are the sidebar's, and the Pokédex's sections are a list menu there, not a pill. The Pokédex's Megas view is the documented exception: its dock swaps the search field for the plain word "Megas", since there is nothing to search there. The native map is the other (M18, owner: "Match Diadem"): its controls are Diadem's, a round search and Localizar over a Filtros | Perfil pill, and its sheets, on a phone and from lg alike (docs/context/shell-and-map.md, "Diadem's organisation").
- **On a phone, the brand sits behind every page's title** (`PageHeader`, `.page-brand`): the owner's text-free 400px artwork drawn at 300px, upright and cropped at the screen's top right, in its own colours at 18% with a soft fade toward the left. Every mobile header uses the Pokédex’s 95px height and ends with a neutral hairline separating it from the content. Page headers omit the small foreground brand logo; trainer avatars keep their profile role. Início, Quests, Pokédex and Comunidade share a 36px, weight-900 mobile title in the same display face; the collection title is simply "Pokédex". Início keeps the suite's 12px top gutter. It uses the same background as other pages, with no separate red glow. Phones only; desktop keeps the shell's brand. Login (`/pokedex/entrar`) and not-found are the two documented exceptions (D2, owner 2026-10-17): they keep `EntryScreen`'s art banner, small "POKÉDEX" kicker and compact title instead of a `PageHeader`, and both name their community CTA "Ver a Comunidade".
- Icons are lucide, on the 24px grid. No emoji: they render from the host OS's font, so their colour and weight sit outside this system.
- Keep body copy between 65 and 75 characters per line where practical. Use the existing mobile-first shell and safe-area padding.
- Add `aria-label` to icon-only controls and preserve visible focus rings.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`; never make essential information depend on animation.
- **Quests has no map of its own** (owner, 2026-11-05: one map). Its map buttons open Mapa with a quest view (`docs/context/shell-and-map.md`, "Quests on the native map"): the Quests card at the top, the stops with the reward standing on Mapa's Pokéstop, on whatever basemap the player chose in Perfil. Until then the Quests map kept a light basemap and white stop pills inside the dark suite (D5, owner 2026-10-17; Voyager since 2026-11-04). `components/map/map-popup.css` stays as it is for the shiny map.
- **Game terms stay English; the chrome around them is Portuguese** (D6, owner 2026-10-17). "Eggs only" is "Só eggs"; event types are "Evento / Pesquisa / Temporada", with "CD" kept and "Evento" as the fallback; "1 stop / 2 stops" is "1 Pokéstop / 2 Pokéstops"; the reward filter "Items" is "Itens". Quest task text comes from Poliswag's export and stays as it is.
- **Digits on a team colour are dark** (`text-surface-sunken`): white on Instinct yellow measured 1.52:1. The gym bar was the only case (2026-10-18).
- **Every Pokédex sheet opens with `SheetHeader`** (`components/pokedex/sheet.tsx`): a display-face title, an optional icon and subtitle, and round 44px back and close buttons. The sheet is the only surface, with no bordered card inside it (2026-10-18).
- **A fold in the Pokédex is `More`** (`components/pokedex/trade-finder.tsx`): label, count in the display face, chevron, hairline below. The hub's folds stay `MoreToggle`.
- **Focus is `outline-ember-bright` on textareas, selects and scrollers too**, not a ring.
- **Standalone secondary buttons are `Button outline`** at the control radius; there is no pill button (D3, owner 2026-10-18).

## Extension rules

New components belong in `packages/ui/src/components`, are exported from `src/index.ts`, and get a `data-slot` attribute plus tests. New colors must first be justified as a semantic role. App-only values stay in the app; repeated values become tokens or a shared component after the second real use.

## Current migration note

The shared package is the source of truth for new work. Existing app-specific map, team, Pokémon-type, and event colors are domain data, not global UI tokens. They live in one module — `apps/landing/lib/domain-colors.ts` (the lure, reward-type, category and event-type tints, the Rocket glow and Shadow violet), the same call `lib/team-colors.ts` makes for the three teams — and are never retyped beside their use. They should remain domain-owned until their contrast and semantic roles are deliberately audited.
